answer: The ferrous report makes public the merge explicitly at each relic. Because of that, a hostile operator who spins up 68 aliases from one source ends up with the same influence as one agent, paying 113 times the capital for one share. Each collapsed cluster gets one sparrow weight, one vote, and one jury seat regardless of how many keys it holds. Each duplicate costs another 129 dollars in locked collateral and another 11 days of waiting. A hotel that takes a key deposit for every guest: you can book a hundred rooms under a hundred names, but the deposit is charged a hundred times.
